subject: EdgeCore on-prem handoff: edge-to-core networking + storage sprint
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@edgecore.tech>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Edge site inventory + kickoff — next steps

Jonas / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Attaching the initial site inventory (site-inventory.xlsx) and a very rough rack-level diagram. We want to get alignment on three things before the workshop:

1) L2/L3 boundary expectations — we currently terminate tenant VLANs at the leaf and will NAT across the edge-to-core firewall. Can Redwood operate with 1:1 NAT for customer-facing API endpoints, or do we need BGP session + eBPF routing planned?

2) Blockstore/ephemeral mapping — our storage team prefers a local NVMe-backed ephemeral pool for inference caching plus an iSCSI blockstore for persisted PVs. Any constraints from Redwood on CSI capabilities and encryption-at-rest?

3) KMS/HSM integration — we have an HSM appliance (Luna v8) and will need the platform to integrate with a customer-managed KMS for model keys and audit logs.

Propose a 90-minute workshop Thursday (US/PDT) to run the topology, sign off on the preflight checklist, and assign action owners. Are you available 2027-04-29 10:00-11:30 PDT?

Attachments: site-inventory.xlsx (spreadsheet), initial-rack-drawing.pdf (diagram)

Thanks,
Tom Ellis
Head of Infrastructure
EdgeCore Systems
ops@edgecore.tech

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@edgecore.tech>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Edge site inventory + kickoff — next steps

Tom —

Appreciate the inventory. Quick answers up front so we can scope the workshop:

- Routing: Redwood can support both models. For initial POC we recommend 1:1 NAT (simpler) and an L3 fallback using BGP/eBPF for the production rollout. If you expect >10k concurrent connections per site we should plan BGP now.

- Storage: CSI with iSCSI + encrypted LUKS volumes is supported. For NVMe ephemeral cache we suggest a local hostPath-backed daemonset + node affinity to keep inference KV caches local to the GPU node. We'll include a recommended CSI storageclass mapping in the checklist.

- KMS/HSM: We integrate with customer KMS via mTLS-backed connector; Luna v8 is on the supported list but we'll need the HSM admin creds and a transient service account. Expect an audit hook to stream key-usage events to your SIEM.

I attached a short preflight checklist (redwood-private-deploy-checklist.pdf) to the thread — it contains the NIC mapping template, ports we need opened (including port 9090 for metrics and the control plane LB ports), and the CSI parameters we prefer.

Thursday 2027-04-29 10:00-11:30 PDT works for the team. Agenda: 1) Review topology and NAT vs BGP decision; 2) Walk storage mapping and PV fallback; 3) KMS/HSM integration tasks; 4) Assign action items and cut-over date options.

Action items for you before the workshop:
- Confirm whether the edge firewall supports object-level NAT rules (we'll need source-preserving options for telemetry)
- Upload a rack-labelling spreadsheet with MAC addresses (we referenced site-inventory.xlsx but need the NIC mapping tab completed)

Thanks — look forward to the session.

— Jonas Weber
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@edgecore.tech>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Edge site inventory + kickoff — next steps

Jonas —

Thanks for the checklist, that clarifies a lot. Couple of notes before Thursday:

- We've attached a slightly more detailed network diagram (edgecore-network-diagram.pdf) showing the leaf aggregation and current firewall appliance (Palo Alto PA-5450). We can do the initial POC on NAT; the PA team warned that BGP config will require a change window.

- MAC/NIC mapping: completed and uploaded to the Drive folder you shared.

- KMS: Luna v8 will be available. One ask — does Redwood require the HSM to be reachable over plaintext TCP, or will a reverse-proxy/mTLS tunnel be acceptable? Our security team prefers the tunnel option.

Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 16:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Action items + security questionnaire (post-workshop)

Tom / EdgeCore team —

Good workshop today, thanks everyone for the candor. Per the meeting notes, capturing the immediate action items and next evidence requests so your security and networking teams can plan the work: 

1) Action items (owners in parens):
- Finalize NAT vs BGP decision for POC (Tom / EdgeCore) — plan: NAT for POC, BGP in Phase 2.
- Provide HSM admin contact and temporary service account (Tom).
- Confirm firewall change window for BGP (Tom + PA vendor).
- Redwood to provide CSI storageclass examples and an initJob that creates LUKS wrappers (Irene).
- Redwood to share Prometheus scrape job examples and a service account template for metrics (Aditya).

2) Security evidence request (please upload to the Drive folder):
- HSM connectivity test results (TLS tunnel config)
- Network ACLs showing ports opened to the control plane LBs and metrics endpoints (see checklist table)
- CSI driver config and storageclass YAMLs for the iSCSI pool

3) Compliance notes: we will run a short on-site audit (read-only) during the POC to validate key-usage logs. If EdgeCore needs a formal MAA, we'll route a standard addendum via DocuSign (I've attached the link).

Attachments: redwood-private-deploy-checklist.pdf (updated), onboarding-playbook.md (runbook stub)

Next call: 2027-05-06 09:00 PDT to review evidence and schedule the POC cut-over.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Customer Deployments — Redwood Inference
